body:
INDEPENDENT INFORMATION-DESIGN / INTERACTION / ACCESSIBILITY REVIEW — codex-mockup-ux-review

Artifact reviewed read-only: `/Users/bbuchsbaum/code/scala/storyatlas4s/mockups/mockup1.png`, 1536x1024, SHA-256 `d136675d7b11e6c1197026483662812f16766bbb71051ffcf9611ad00fb3d6ce`.

Disposition: a strong composition sketch that makes synchronized focus tangible, but not an acceptable default workspace yet. I agree with every scientific/evidence blocker in the parent review. The points below are additive UX and accessibility findings.

WHAT THE MOCKUP GETS RIGHT

- The repeated Scene 2.3 focus across overview, Codex, feature tracks, and recall is the clearest part of the composition. It begins to communicate one identity system viewed through several representations.
- The structural tree beside genuine-looking paginated text, the page/source footer, and the selected-event inspector are a credible evidentiary reading workflow.
- Overview plus detail in recall is useful, as are explicit legends and named presets. The mockup gives analysts visible ways to orient rather than assuming they understand an unlabeled canvas.

INFORMATION HIERARCHY AND SPLIT-WORKSPACE THESIS

1. The top tabs say Atlas, Codex, Analysis, and Recall are mutually exclusive modes, yet the selected Codex screen displays all four at once. That contradiction makes it unclear whether the tabs switch workspaces, set a lens, or merely move focus.
2. The canonical text is visually subordinate. The story map and recall surfaces together take most of the useful area, while the readable text is a small light rectangle inside a dense left stack. The intended default should be a persistent Codex plus one replaceable projection, with the inspector collapsible or dockable. Recall should replace the map when active rather than joining it by default.
3. Nearly every box has the same border weight and contrast, so there is no strong primary, secondary, and tertiary hierarchy. A selected event should dominate; overview tracks and global controls should recede.
4. Feature information is repeated in the bird-eye overview and the sensory-track panel without declaring distinct roles. Keep both only if one is explicitly a navigation aggregate and the other a measurement view with scale, coverage, and receipt.
5. Notes, bookmarks, export, presets, multiple legends, filters, map controls, page controls, and lens pills all compete at the same level. Secondary commands should move into contextual menus or a single utility bar.

EXACT-TEXT READABILITY AND ANNOTATION BUDGET

6. At 1536x1024, much of the interface text appears around 10–12 px and the source prose itself is small. The page should begin at a comfortable reading size, permit font and line-spacing enlargement, and stay usable when the canvas is collapsed or the browser is zoomed.
7. Saturated full-line background bands compete with letterforms and make exact prose harder to scan. Normal reading mode should show at most one restrained scalar wash; other annotations should use gutters, underlines, or selection-only disclosure. The system needs an annotation-channel budget that is enforced by presets: one structural hierarchy, one relation family, one scalar feature, and optionally one comparison overlay.
8. The narrow icon strip beside every line is visually cryptic and creates many tiny targets. Icons require text alternatives, tooltips that are not the sole explanation, keyboard access, and a target size meeting WCAG 2.2 requirements.
9. A quiet reading preset must be first-class, not merely a button at the bottom: exact selectable DOM text, hierarchy optionally visible, no inferred claims, and no decorative metrics.

SHARED FOCUS AND SEMANTIC ZOOM

10. The white focus rectangles are promising, but their meaning is ambiguous: viewport, selected span, query result, or brush? Use one named shared-focus state with a breadcrumb such as `Story > Episode 2 > Scene 2.3 > Event`, a persistent selected-object treatment, and an explicit statement that each rectangle is the same focus projected into that surface.
11. The map zoom control currently suggests geometric zoom only. Nothing in the sketch shows episode territories subdividing into scenes, scenes into events, or events opening into propositions while identity persists. Add visible semantic-level cues and an LOD breadcrumb; do not call enlargement of the same node-link graph semantic zoom.
12. Text page turns are pagination, not semantic zoom. Page navigation and the representation-level ladder should remain distinct.
13. Projection changes and fly-to transitions need a reduced-motion mode. Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, preserve selection and focus with an immediate change or short crossfade; never require motion to understand object correspondence.

COLOR AND NONVISUAL ACCESS

14. Color carries too many unrelated meanings. Purple denotes location nodes and auditory annotation; yellow appears for goals, prose bands, and recall misordering; green denotes characters, exact recall links, and omission symbols. Either reserve globally stable meanings or make legends visibly projection-local, but do not let the same hue silently change ontology within one screen.
15. Node categories need redundant shape or icon coding; relation families need pattern plus labels; selection needs more than a hue change. The red/green recall semantics must remain distinguishable under common color-vision deficiencies and in grayscale.
16. Several dim gray labels, thin plot lines, and small glyphs on the dark background appear likely to be difficult at low vision. The implementation needs measured WCAG contrast checks, 200 percent browser-zoom checks for the DOM regions, and a grayscale/color-blind review rather than visual intuition alone.
17. Exact prose, controls, tree, and inspector should be semantic DOM. Graphics need an accessible alternative: a navigable list or table of visible marks and relations, not thousands of raw SVG nodes in the screen-reader tree. Selection changes should announce object type, label, evidence span, epistemic status, and available actions in a controlled live region.
18. Provide a complete keyboard route: move through the structural tree, enter the text, next/previous annotation, open evidence, move to the corresponding Atlas object, return to the exact span, and change projection without losing focus. Drag and scroll instructions cannot be the only way to brush or zoom. Every hover preview needs focus and explicit-open equivalents.
19. `Show Labels` appears unchecked while every graph node already has a label. If it means edge labels or secondary labels, name it precisely. Ambiguous state controls are especially costly in a dense scientific interface.

COGNITIVE LOAD AND MAP SEMANTICS

20. The map remains a global node-link graph, and `Layout: Chronological` suggests meaningful geometry while x, y, and distance meanings are absent. The projection contract must be visible next to the map. If distance is uninterpreted, say so. If chronology owns x, show the axis. Containment regions and local detail would better support the Atlas thesis than displaying every ontology family in one graph.
21. The currently selected event is not visually unmistakable in the map. Give selection a high-contrast halo/outline and dim nonfocus material without implying scientific unimportance.
22. The default screen tries to support reading, global structure, feature exploration, causal inspection, and recall adjudication simultaneously. A task-centered preset should expose one question at a time and make hidden layers discoverable without making them constantly visible.

RECOMMENDED NEXT COMPOSITION

- A thin, full-width discourse overview/feature rail.
- Below it, a persistent Codex occupying roughly half the workspace and one replaceable projection occupying the other half.
- A collapsible claim inspector tied to the current selection.
- Recall as a projection/workspace that replaces the Atlas pane, with its matrix first and route tracer on demand.
- One clearly identified shared focus and one active quantitative feature with receipt/missingness disclosure.
- Responsive variants at 1536x1024, 1280x800, and 200 percent browser zoom; a grayscale variant; and annotated keyboard focus order.

Acceptance test for a revised mockup: an analyst should be able to identify the exact source passage, selected narrative object, active projection contract, active feature and aggregation, and next keyboard action in a few seconds without reading every panel. The current artifact demonstrates the ambition, but its default density conceals that chain.
